references.text: Pharaoh orders that straw not be given to the Israelites, yet demands the same amount of bricks - the background for the taskmasters' pressure in verse 13
The taskmasters and foremen convey Pharaoh's command that the people must gather their own straw, but the daily quota remains unchanged
The consequence of the taskmasters' pressure - Israelite foremen are beaten because the daily quota was not met
The Lord sees the oppression of the Israelites by the taskmasters (נֹגְשִׂים) - the same word is used here
The earlier slavery and forced labor imposed on the Israelites in Egypt
Isaiah uses נֹגְשִׂים (oppressors/taskmasters) to refer to those who oppress God's people
The prophecy of deliverance from the taskmaster's rod (נֹגֵשׂ) - the same root as in Exodus 5:13
Describes the same historical context and elaborates on the nature of the slavery that led to the demand for straw.
Direct narrative precursor; verse 7 explains the reason for the requirement to complete the work without straw in verse 13.
